match.reason: The closest bank point, The periodic table's layout, covers groups, periods and atomic-number order, but it does not teach the brief's electron basis (same outer electrons in a group, a new shell in each period), and adding that would be a new step rather than a small change.

draft.title: Groups and periods
card: The periodic table lists elements in order of atomic number, which is the number of protons in an atom. Atomic number rises by one from each element to the next.
a column of the table. Elements in a group have the same number of electrons in their outer shell, so they react in similar ways.
a row of the table. Moving along a row, atomic number rises and outer electrons are added to the same shell.
A new period starts when a new shell begins to fill. The period number is the number of shells that hold electrons. For example, sodium is in period 3, so its atoms have three shells with electrons.
draft.remember: Group: same outer electrons, similar reactions. Period: the number of shells in use.

a.q: Lithium, sodium and potassium are in the same group. What does this tell you about their atoms?
opts: They have the same number of outer electrons
They have the same number of protons
They have the same number of electron shells
They have the same atomic number
a.why: Elements in a group have the same number of outer electrons, which is why they react alike. Shells are the tempting option, but the number of shells matches for elements in the same period, not the same group.
a.clue: Think about what a column shares, and what decides how atoms react.

b.q: Mia finds an element in period 4 of the periodic table. Which statement about its atoms must be true?
opts: Electrons are found in four shells
Electrons are found in three shells
There are four electrons in the outer shell
There are four protons in the nucleus
b.why: The period number is the number of shells that hold electrons, so a period 4 atom has four shells. Four outer electrons is tempting, but outer electrons are linked to the group, not the period.
b.clue: A period is a row. Ask what a new row stands for.

a.best: They have the same number of outer electrons

b.best: Electrons are found in four shells
